newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks notch 6-yr high as electronics soar.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks notch 6-yr high as electronics soar.

text.p: Taiwan share prices edged up slightly to yet another six-year high on Saturday, spurred by strong buying interest in fundamentals-backed electronic shares, Taiwan's brokers said.
The weighted index closed a scant 15.74 points or 0.19 percent higher at 8,291.31, largely on the strength of a 2.55 percent surge in the electronics sector.

Saturday's close surpassed the 8,275.57 finish on March 14 to marked the index's highest close since it reached 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990. Turnover was hectic at T$137.9 billion in the abbreviated two-hour weekend session.
"Electronics were the stars of the day," said George Hou, a fund manager for Jardine Fleming.
"Buying interest came from both institutional and individual investors who believe electronics companies will show strong performance during the second quarter," Hou said.
Semiconductor issue United Micro, gained T$1.6 or 3.27 percent to T$50.5 in active trade. Computer giant Acer Inc rose by T$3 or 4.48 percent to T$70.
But shipping shares -- which had risen recently on growing hopes of imminent direct sailings between Taiwan and China to end a ban dating to 1949 -- ended lower on profit-taking.
Yang Ming Marine, widely tipped to be a China shipping pioneer, lost 80 cents or 1.96 percent to T$40.1.
Brokers saw more room for further gains next week, but noted the index would soon approach its resistance of 8,450 points.
"Sentiment will be cautious next week," said Hou of Jardine Fleming.
Political tensions arisng from a controversial March 22-27 visit by Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, were likely to drive investors to the sidelines, brokers said.
"People are worried about the impact of the Dalai Lama's visit. No one can predict mainland China's reaction," Hou said.
